candidates.credit: "Göbekli Tepe Birthing Women.jpg" – Bernietaylor, CC BY 4.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe_Birthing_Women.jpg)
candidates.text: File:Göbekli Tepe Birthing Women.jpg Göbekli Tepe artifacts representing birthing scenes. The Göbekli Tepe statuette has one feline on her left shoulder. Her other side has been sintered. The woman on the slab is flanked by two lion pillars.

candidates.credit: "Göbekli Tepe Birthing Woman.jpg" – Bernietaylor, CC BY 4.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe_Birthing_Woman.jpg)
candidates.text: File:Göbekli Tepe Birthing Woman.jpg Göbekli Tepe engraving of an away facing squatting woman giving birth shown in comparison to a side view squat birth position. Below the Göbekli Tepe birthing woman are her birth tissue and placenta. Dated to more than 10,000 years ago.

candidates.credit: "Göbekli Tepe Birthing Woman in Leopard Pillar Building.jpg" – Bernietaylor, CC BY 4.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe_Birthing_Woman_in_Leopard_Pillar_Building.jpg)
candidates.text: File:Göbekli Tepe Birthing Woman in Leopard Pillar Building.jpg Engraving of squatting woman between two Leopard Pillars at Göbekli Tepe, Turkey. The woman is facing away from the viewer and in a birthing position. This Neolithic artifact is dated to more than 10,000 years ago.
